positions.as_written: Examine the anterior cruciate in any complete medial injury.
Treat bracing as a mechanical intervention aimed at healing position, and explain it that way.
Treat medial laxity as a question about length rather than continuity.
Delay the decision in an isolated medial injury where the anatomy says healing is likely, and re-examine rather than operating on the first finding.
Assess alignment before reconstructing chronic medial laxity, since a valgus limb protects a medial reconstruction and a varus one does not.
Consider shortening rather than only reattaching in a chronic injury, because the problem is length.
Avoid reading continuity on imaging as competence.
